opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jennifer Martin (employee ID E033) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E033.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Employee is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin to Payroll, but admin is only allowed when the employee's role owns the system; Payroll is owned by Payroll Specialist. Granting max allowed level of write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB records E033 as a contractor with basic security training (note from prior memory saying full-time appears inaccurate per Security DB). Contractors with basic training are limited to read; admin is never allowed for contractors. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: E033's employment record per Security DB is contractor with basic security training (HR's note listing full-time is identified as inaccurate). Contractors are never granted admin. With basic security training, the maximum allowed access is read. The requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, so the maximum of read is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee: Jennifer Martin (E033)
Request: admin access to Payroll

Two notes from HR and Security with conflicting information:

HR note: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation: write. HR says admin not allowed because role doesn't own system (Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist). Grant max write.

Security note: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read. Security says contractor with basic training limited to read; admin never for contractors.

Hmm, conflicting info about employment type. HR says full_time, Security says contractor (and claims prior memory saying full-time is inaccurate per Security DB).

Access policy:
- full_time: up to write. Admin only if role owns system. Analyst doesn't own Payroll (Payroll Specialist owns it). So max would be write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Basic training → read. Never admin.

So under HR's version: max write → grant write (requested admin > max).
Under Security's version: max read → grant read.

Which to trust? The security DB records the employment type. Security agent says the DB indicates contractor, and that the prior memory saying full-time is inaccurate. Typically in these scenarios, the Security agent's DB info is authoritative for employment type. Let me think carefully.

The team memory notes: security agent says "Security DB records E033 as a contractor with basic security training (note from prior memory saying full-time appears inaccurate per Security DB)."

Hmm, which is correct? We need to decide based on available info. The Security note explicitly says the HR note's full-time is inaccurate. The security records are probably more authoritative for employment status. Also the security training basic → contractor limited to read.

So the maximum level is read. Requested admin > max, so grant max = read.

I'll submit decision: read.

Evidence: Employee's actual employment type is contractor per Security DB with basic security training. Contractors never get admin; with basic training, max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read.
